simple.meaning: אֱלִישָׁה (ʼĔlîyshâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Elishah , a son of Javan.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֱלִישָׁה (H473) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 10:4, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Chronicles, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֱלִישָׁה (H473) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֱלִישָׁה (H473) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֱלִישָׁה (ʼĔlîyshâh) / H473 is traced through Genesis 10:4, 1 Chronicles 1:7, Ezekiel 27:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H473. Elishah אֲלִישָׁה proper name, of a location as son of Javan Gen 10:4 ; 1Chr 1:7 ; א ׳אִיֵּי Ezek 27:7 ( Aeolis Josephus Jerome Kn; H. Derenbourg Mélanges Graux, 235 f (English translation Hebraica . Oct. 1887, 7) ; Hellas ᵑ7 Jon etc., Len Orig. ii. 2. 34 f ; Italy , with Sicily , compare ᵑ7 אִיטַלְיָא מְדִינַת Ezek, Di Gen 10:4 ; Carthage = Elissa, Sta De Populo Javan, 8 f ; EMey Geschichte i. § 282 ; decision difficult; last view very attractive). I. [ אלל ] ( to be weak or insufficient , assumed in Thes as root of אֱלִיל (as also of אַל ): compare Arabic to fail in a thing).
